# The Astronomy Space

> An educational astronomy website covering the Solar System, stars, galaxies, nebulae, constellations, and stargazing guides. Features interactive components including atmospheric layer explorers, an axial tilt visualiser, lunar eclipse simulator, tidal forces diagram, Mars weight calculator, and a light-speed delay simulator. All articles are fact-checked and written for a general audience.

## Solar System

- [The Solar System Overview](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/) : Hub page — planets, dwarf planets, the Sun, and our cosmic neighbourhood
- [The Sun](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/sun/) : Solar structure, nuclear fusion, sunspots, solar wind, and the heliosphere
- [Mercury](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/mercury/) : Smallest planet — extreme temperature swings, heavily cratered surface, no atmosphere
- [Venus](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/venus/) : Earth's twin — crushing CO₂ atmosphere, runaway greenhouse effect, retrograde rotation
- [Earth](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/earth/) : Complete guide — atmosphere (interactive layers), axial tilt, magnetic field, geology, and why Earth supports life
- [The Moon](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/earth/moon/) : Lunar phases (interactive), tidal forces, lunar eclipses, Apollo missions, tidal locking
- [Mars](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/mars/) : The Red Planet — geology, Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, atmospheric layers (interactive), water history, rovers, weight calculator, light-speed delay simulator
- [Jupiter](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/jupiter/) : King of planets — Great Red Spot, magnetosphere, Galilean moons, Juno mission
- [Saturn](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/saturn/) : Ring system, Titan, Enceladus geysers, Cassini mission
- [Uranus](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/uranus/) : Ice giant with 98° axial tilt — ring system, Miranda, Voyager 2 flyby
- [Neptune](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/solar-system/neptune/) : Outermost planet — supersonic winds, Great Dark Spot, Triton

## Small Bodies

- [Small Bodies Overview](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/small-bodies/) : Comets, asteroids, dwarf planets, and meteors
- [Asteroids](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/small-bodies/asteroids/) : Rocky Solar System remnants — Asteroid Belt, C/S/M types, near-Earth objects, planetary defence, DART mission
- [Comets](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/small-bodies/comets/) : Icy wanderers — nucleus, coma, tails; Halley's Comet, Rosetta mission, Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud origin
- [Dwarf Planets](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/small-bodies/dwarf-planets/) : IAU 2006 definition; Pluto, Eris, Ceres, Makemake, Haumea
- [Meteors & Meteorites](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/small-bodies/meteors/) : Meteoroid/meteor/meteorite distinction, major showers, Chelyabinsk 2013, Chicxulub

## Stars

- [Stars Overview](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/) : Stellar classification, HR diagram, and stellar evolution
- [Main Sequence Stars](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/main-sequence/) : Hydrogen-burning majority — spectral types O through M
- [Red Giants](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/red-giants/) : Post-main-sequence evolution — helium burning, planetary nebula precursors
- [White Dwarfs](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/white-dwarfs/) : Dense stellar remnants — Chandrasekhar limit, Type Ia supernovae
- [Neutron Stars](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/neutron-stars/) : Extreme-density remnants — pulsars, magnetars
- [Black Holes](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/black-holes/) : Event horizons, singularities, Hawking radiation, Sagittarius A*, gravitational waves
- [Supergiants](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/supergiants/) : Stellar behemoths — Betelgeuse, Rigel, supernova progenitors
- [Binary Star Systems](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/binary-systems/) : Stellar pairs — types, mass transfer, novae
- [Variable Stars](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/stars/variable-stars/) : Cepheids, RR Lyrae, eclipsing binaries, distance ladder

## Planets (Types & Classification)

- [Planets Overview](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/) : Planetary classification — terrestrial, gas giants, ice giants, dwarf planets, exoplanets, and exotic types
- [Terrestrial Planets](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/terrestrial-planets/) : Rocky worlds — Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars; iron cores, silicate mantles, thin atmospheres
- [Gas Giants](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/gas-giants/) : Jupiter and Saturn — hydrogen/helium composition, Great Red Spot, ring systems, Galilean moons
- [Ice Giants](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/ice-giants/) : Uranus and Neptune — methane-rich atmospheres, extreme axial tilts, supersonic winds
- [Dwarf Planets](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/dwarf-planets/) : IAU definition, Pluto's reclassification, Eris, Haumea, Makemake, Ceres, Kuiper Belt context
- [Exoplanets](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/exoplanets/) : Worlds orbiting other stars — transit/RV/imaging detection, 5,700+ confirmed, JWST, habitability
- [Super-Earths](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/super-earths/) : 1–10 Earth masses — rocky vs. mini-Neptune ambiguity, radius gap, Kepler-22b, 55 Cancri e
- [Hot Jupiters](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/hot-jupiters/) : Gas giants in <10-day orbits — tidal locking, puffed atmospheres, 51 Pegasi b, WASP-12b
- [Rogue Planets](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/planets/rogue-planets/) : Free-floating worlds unbound to any star — ejection mechanisms, microlensing detection, estimated trillions

## Deep Sky Objects

- [Galaxies](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/) : Spiral, elliptical, and irregular galaxies — formation, classification, the Milky Way
- [Spiral Galaxies](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/spiral/) : Disk galaxies with sweeping arms — density waves, Hubble classification, Andromeda, Whirlpool, star formation in arms
- [Elliptical Galaxies](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/elliptical/) : Smooth spheroidal systems of old stars — E0–E7 classification, M87, galaxy mergers, AGN feedback, dark matter halos
- [Irregular Galaxies](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/irregular/) : Galaxies without regular structure — Magellanic Clouds, starburst systems, tidal disruption, Antennae Galaxies
- [Lenticular Galaxies](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/lenticular/) : Disk galaxies without spiral arms — S0 classification, retired spirals, ram-pressure stripping, NGC 5866 Spindle Galaxy
- [Dwarf Galaxies](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/dwarf/) : Small low-luminosity galaxies — dark matter dominance, Sagittarius Dwarf, Local Group satellites, missing satellites problem
- [The Milky Way](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/milky-way/) : Our home barred spiral galaxy — Sagittarius A*, spiral arms, Gaia mission, dark matter halo, Andromeda collision
- [Active Galaxies](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/active/) : Galaxies powered by accreting supermassive black holes — quasars, Seyfert galaxies, blazars, AGN unified model, AGN feedback
- [Galaxy Clusters](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/galaxies/clusters/) : Largest gravitationally bound structures — Virgo and Coma Clusters, intracluster medium, dark matter, Bullet Cluster, gravitational lensing
- [Nebulae Overview](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/) : All nebula types — emission, reflection, dark, planetary, supernova remnants, HII regions, molecular clouds, protoplanetary
- [Emission Nebulae](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/emission/) : Ionized gas glowing in H-alpha and [OIII] — Orion Nebula, Eagle Nebula, Lagoon Nebula, Carina Nebula
- [Reflection Nebulae](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/reflection/) : Dust clouds scattering starlight blue — Pleiades nebula, Witch Head Nebula, Iris Nebula
- [Dark Nebulae](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/dark/) : Dense dust blocking background light — Horsehead Nebula, Barnard 68, Bok globules, stellar nurseries
- [Planetary Nebulae](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/planetary/) : Shells ejected by dying low-mass stars — Ring Nebula, Helix Nebula, Cat's Eye Nebula, central white dwarfs
- [Supernova Remnants](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/supernova-remnants/) : Expanding shells from massive star explosions — Crab Nebula, Cassiopeia A, Veil Nebula, synchrotron radiation
- [HII Regions](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/hii-regions/) : Vast star-forming ionized hydrogen clouds — Tarantula Nebula, Strömgren spheres, OB star clusters
- [Molecular Clouds](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/molecular-clouds/) : Cold dense H₂/CO clouds (~10 K) — Pillars of Creation, Giant Molecular Clouds, Jeans instability
- [Protoplanetary Nebulae](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/nebulae/protoplanetary/) : Short-lived AGB-to-PN transition phase — Egg Nebula, Red Rectangle, bipolar morphology
- [Constellations](https://theastronomy.space/atlas/constellations/) : All 88 IAU constellations — mythology, star patterns, celestial navigation

## Stargazing Guides

- [Stargazing in Scandinavia](https://theastronomy.space/chronicles/stargazing/scandinavia/) : Dark sky sites, Northern Lights, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Iceland
- [Stargazing in England](https://theastronomy.space/chronicles/stargazing/england/) : Dark sky reserves, light pollution, seasonal highlights across the UK
- [Stargazing in India](https://theastronomy.space/chronicles/stargazing/india/) : Dark sky sites across India — Hanle Dark Sky Reserve, Ladakh, Spiti Valley, Rann of Kutch, permits and planning
- [Stargazing in China](https://theastronomy.space/chronicles/stargazing/china/) : Dark sky sites across China — Tibet Ali Dark Sky Reserve, Qinghai salt lakes, Xinjiang desert, Tibetan Plateau, permits and planning
- [Stargazing in Germany](https://theastronomy.space/chronicles/stargazing/germany/) : Dark sky parks across Germany — Eifel National Park, Westhavelland, Rhön Biosphere Reserve, Bavarian Forest, aurora from northern Germany
- [Stargazing in Poland](https://theastronomy.space/chronicles/stargazing/poland/) : Dark sky sites across Poland — Bieszczady Mountains, Tatra Mountains, Białowieża Primeval Forest, Masuria Lake District, eastern plains
